title: nyc-live · morning review
subtitle: Lower Manhattan in 3D, built overnight. Each feature opens its own view: use the **Open** link, then the links in the steps. Every view is in the URL, so a note you send carries it. *Recorded* mode plays the MTA feed saved on Oct 18 at 7:02 PM ET; *live* mode needs the dev server to reach the MTA, Citi Bike and the Decisions API.

features.title: The stage view: trains under the venue, at night
features.intro: Everything together on the Venue preset at night: buildings, streets, the subway with its trains, Citi Bike, and an answered question.
steps: Open the view with the link above. The red **598 Broadway** pin and its ring are in the middle, lit for night, with the label just above the pin.

Coloured subway lines run below the streets around the pin, and short, thick blocks in line colours (trains) move along them: at this moment of the recording, two yellow trains and an orange one pass right by the venue. Lines show faintly through the buildings too.
The **Ask the city** panel shows *What is the fastest way from 598 Broadway to Brooklyn Bridge?*, an answer with a percentage, and **recorded** at its top right.
The status at the top left says the train positions *may not be real time* and stays clear of the panel.
features.pass: Trains are visible under the venue, the panel answers the route question from the recorded feed, and the status line and the panel do not overlap.

features.title: Buildings
features.intro: Real footprints and roof heights from NYC Open Data, extruded and coloured by height.
steps: Open the view. Dense blocks of buildings of different heights surround the pin, and the venue's own building is highlighted in yellow (`sel=bin:1007945` in the URL).
Click another building. It turns yellow instead, and the URL's `sel=` changes to that building's BIN.
Open [the whole area from the Battery](/#cam=-2297.9,750,3512.9&tgt=-1668.1,0,2376.8&mode=recorded&t=2026-10-18T23:02:17Z). Every building from the Battery to 17th Street draws within a few seconds.
features.pass: Buildings stand at their real heights, one click selects one building, and the full area loads in under 5 s.
features.note: The full area needs the downloaded data on the dev server (`node scripts/fetch-buildings.ts`). Without it the status line says *fixture only* and only the blocks around the venue draw.

features.title: Ground, water and streets
features.intro: Manhattan's shoreline from NYC Open Data, water around it, and the street centrelines.
steps: Open the view, straight down with north at the top. Land fills the middle, with the Hudson on the left and the East River on the right.
Thin street lines form the blocks; there is no even square grid anywhere.
Open [the same view at night](/#cam=0,3500,1&tgt=0,0,0&mode=fixture&light=night). Land and water darken, and the streets stay bright.
features.pass: Land is bordered by water on both sides, the street grid is real, and night keeps the streets readable.

features.title: Subway network
features.intro: Every line in the area from the MTA's static GTFS, as tubes 12 m below the street in its route colour, with stations.
steps: Open the view, straight down on the venue. Lines in at least three colours run under the streets; the yellow N/Q/R/W passes right by the pin; small white markers are stations.
Click a line. It brightens, the others dim, and the URL gets `sel=route:…`. Click empty ground to clear it.
Open [the whole island from above at night](/#cam=74.4,3497.9,944.3&tgt=-32.4,0,885.1&mode=recorded&t=2026-10-18T23:02:17Z&light=night). Every line shows in its own colour across lower Manhattan.
features.pass: The lines read in their colours from close and from high up, by day and at night, and a click selects one.

features.title: Trains
features.intro: Trains from the MTA's realtime feeds, placed on the lines from their predicted stop times and moving between stops.
steps: Open the view. Short blocks in line colours sit on the subway lines and move slowly along them, and the URL's `t=` moves on with them, so a note reopens the moment you saw.
The status line says *MTA data from Oct 18, 7:02 PM ET: positions may not be real time*.
Open [the Venue in live mode](/#cam=320,420,620&tgt=0,0,0&mode=live). The trains are where the MTA says they are now, and the not-real-time notice is gone.
features.pass: Trains move along their own lines, and old data is labelled as possibly not real time.
features.note: The live step needs the dev server to reach the MTA's feeds. If it cannot, the status line names the feeds it is missing.

features.title: Citi Bike
features.intro: One bar per dock, as tall as the bikes available, with e-bikes stacked on top in a second colour.
steps: Open the view (only the ground, the docks and the pin). Bars of different heights stand at street corners around the pin, blue below and green on top.
Open [the live docks](/#cam=320,420,620&tgt=0,0,0&mode=live&layers=ground,citibike,venue). Around 235 docks stand across the area, their heights from the feed right now.
features.pass: Docks stand at street corners and their heights change with the bikes available.
features.note: The live step needs the dev server to reach the Citi Bike feed.

features.title: Ask the city
features.intro: Typed questions answered by the Decisions API from the city's state, with probabilities, and the answer highlighted in the scene.
steps: Open the view. The panel on the right shows the Brooklyn Bridge question, its answer with a percentage, the other options, and **fixture data** at the top right.

In the panel choose **Fastest way to…** and **Union Square**, then press **Ask**. An answer appears within a second or two, its subway line lights up in the scene while the others dim, and the URL gets `sel=route:…`.
Choose **Is a line running normally?**, pick **F**, press **Ask**. The answer gives the probability that it is (the fixture has the F delayed).

Open [the same question in recorded mode](/#cam=320,420,620&tgt=0,0,0&mode=recorded&t=2026-10-18T23:02:17Z&ask=route:brooklyn-bridge). The panel says **recorded**: the answer now comes from the trains in the saved feed.
Open [the same question live](/#cam=320,420,620&tgt=0,0,0&mode=live&ask=route:brooklyn-bridge). The panel says **live**: the answer comes from the trains and Citi Bike docks right now.
features.pass: Every question gets an answer with a percentage, the answer is highlighted in the scene, and recorded and live mode answer from their own data, not the fixture.
features.note: Needs `OPENAI_API_KEY` in the dev server's environment. Without it the panel says the server has no key; mark this feature blocked.

features.title: Camera, labels and controls
features.intro: Five camera presets with a smooth flight, layer toggles, day and night, and place labels readable on a projector.
steps: Open the view. The toolbar shows **Venue** highlighted; place labels such as *598 Broadway* and *SoHo* sit over the map without overlapping.
Press **Battery**, **Brooklyn Bridge**, **From above** and **Street level** in turn. The camera flies to each, and the pressed one is highlighted. Street level looks up the middle of Broadway.
Press **Night**, then **Day**. Turn **Buildings** off and on. Each change shows in the URL straight away.
Drag the map fast and let go. Within a quarter of a second the URL's `cam=` follows the camera while it still glides; open [the Venue again](/#cam=320,420,620&tgt=0,0,0&mode=fixture) to come back.
features.pass: Every preset, toggle and the day/night switch works and is reflected in the URL, also while the camera is still moving.
features.note: On a touch screen: one finger pans, two fingers rotate and zoom.

features.title: Review notes from the app
features.intro: This panel itself: a note pinned on the scene reaches the reviewer agent with a screenshot and the view's URL.
steps: Open the view. Click **Add comment** in this panel and allow sharing this tab.
Click the venue's yellow building to drop a pin, write a short note and press **Send**.
The panel confirms the note was sent. The agent's copy carries this page's URL, whose hash is the view above, and a screenshot of the scene with the pin drawn on it.
features.pass: The note arrives with the comment, the view's URL and a screenshot of the scene (not of this panel).
features.note: If the screenshot shows this panel instead of the scene, say so in the note: it is a known timing issue of tab capture.
